scope: First draft only, based on the saved research. Goal: make the existing shared communication contract the production path while preserving workflow authority and resumable work. Milestone 1 — adoption: (1) Route final outcomes, comments, questions, artifact references and applicable workflow contributions from Research, Plan, Implement, Validate and Spike through shared validation and receipts; connect MCP, helper and structured terminal adapters. (2) Supply explicit prior-result snapshots or scoped reads, stable IDs/base revisions and historical receipts; handle merged sparse updates, rejections, retries and missing/malformed output after failure, cancellation or interruption. (3) Finish production MCP wiring: authorized comments, existing gated owner-approved creation, recovery after uncertain publication, and visible run-scoped advisory progress including Research/Spike with terminal cleanup. (4) Update canonical instructions, installed bundles and docs; map auxiliary classifier/scheduler/conflict version/error conventions where useful without replacing their typed payloads; verify cold starts, continuation, stale revisions, retries, failure handling and restricted Validate behavior. Milestone 2 — retirement: inventory and give separate dispositions to Plan v1 file handoff, Implement event-file ingress, Validate v1 parser and unreachable Markdown story discovery; remove exclusive dead code and retire supported legacy ingress only after supported upgrade/completion and pending-effect drain are verified. Preserve shared StoryProgress recovery/delivery, live v2 Plan publication, required historical reads/migrations and persisted workflow versions.
decisions: Keep this a simple saved draft, without publishing or freezing engineering stories. Production wiring of the already-built MCP services belongs in #264, following the owner's earlier steering. Reuse existing shared services, transports and native integrations. Adoption and verified removal are distinct milestones. Validate retains its restricted execution and structured terminal assessment; progress never grants acceptance or completion. Keep #274/#296 as the separate intentionally open authentic-host verification track. No new MCP server or MCP-specific business logic; vendor stdout, usage transcripts, process diagnostics and artifact contents remain outside the business-result schema. Future installed-instruction work needs independent protected-tree stories following shared-source work.
assumptions: Use existing authorization semantics for comment targets and gated, exact-content owner approval for creation; detailed presentation decisions can be settled during implementation-ready planning. Supported legacy cohorts and pending effects have not yet been inventoried, so removal safety is unproven. Content/submission upgrades do not change workflow v1; combined-verification retirement requires a separate explicit decision. If supported legacy work cannot drain, explicitly revise the promised removal scope and prepare a focused retirement follow-up rather than reporting retirement complete. Repository tests will prove production composition and recovery behavior; synthetic results will not substitute for authentic host evidence retained under #274/#296.
